prompt.en: According to the commentary, keeping a supplication hidden is recommended and stands nearer to being answered.

explanation.en: Retelling Zechariah's secret cry, the passage says a concealed supplication is what is recommended and is nearer to being answered, so hiding a prayer is presented as the better way.

anchor.quote: concealing a supplication is what is recommended and is nearer to being answered

prompt.en: The passage says Zechariah's request for an heir divides the commentators. What do they divide over?

options.en: Whether the inheritance meant is property or prophethood
Whether Zechariah truly feared his kinsmen
Whether John was born before or after his father
Whether Zechariah's wife was ever truly barren

explanation.en: The passage says the request for an heir divides the commentators: one reading takes the inheritance as property, the other as prophethood, so the split is over what kind of inheritance Zechariah meant.

anchor.quote: The request for 'an heir who may inherit from me' divides the commentators

prompt.en: "That is Yahya ibn Zakariyya, who had no namesake before him; and likewise Husayn had no namesake before him." Who said this?

explanation.en: Glossing the son with no namesake, Imam al-Sadiq pairs Yahya ibn Zakariyya with Husayn, saying each had no namesake before him and the sky wept over none but the two.

anchor.quote: That is Yahya ibn Zakariyya, who had no namesake before him; and likewise Husayn had no namesake before him

prompt.en: When John would say, 'O my Lord,' God, mighty and majestic, would answer, '____, O John.'

explanation.en: Explaining God's tenderness to John, the narration says that whenever John called 'O my Lord,' God answered 'Here I am, O John,' which is how that tenderness showed itself.

anchor.quote: When John would say, 'O my Lord,' God, mighty and majestic, would answer, 'Here I am, O John.'

prompt.en: According to the passage, why is John given peace on the day he is born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive?

options.en: They mark the days of John's prophethood
They are the times a person is most desolate
They are the holiest days of the year
They are when he held to the Book

explanation.en: The passage explains that a person is most desolate at birth, at death, and at resurrection, so peace is placed on John precisely on those three days.

anchor.quote: The most desolate this creature ever is comes in three places

prompt.en: According to the note, how did the Spirit that came to Mary appear to her?

options.en: As a well-proportioned man while remaining an angel
As a fully human being he had become
As a shaft of light with no form
As an old and frail traveler

explanation.en: The note corrects the verse's image of an incarnate human: the Spirit is Gabriel, who took the form of a well-made man while remaining an angel in himself and never actually becoming a human being.

anchor.quote: He appeared to her in the form of a sound, well-made man while remaining an angel in himself, not becoming a human being

prompt.en: She was told to eat, drink, and vow a fast of ____.

explanation.en: The verse has Mary vow a fast and not speak; the passage explains that her fast was silence, a guarding of the tongue rather than only abstaining from food and drink.

anchor.quote: She was told to eat, drink, and vow a fast of silence.

prompt.en: "On that day he was a prophet, a proof of God though not a messenger." Who said this of the infant Jesus?

explanation.en: Asked about the infant who spoke, Imam al-Baqir said that on that day Jesus was a prophet and a proof of God, though not yet a messenger, since the earth is never without such a proof.

anchor.quote: On that day he was a prophet, a proof of God though not a messenger

prompt.en: In the note on verse 34, who are the ones said to be in doubt concerning Jesus?

options.en: The angels who witnessed his birth
Those who dispute and quarrel over him
The prophets who came before him

explanation.en: The note glosses the closing summary: that is Jesus gathers all that was told of him, and those in doubt are the people who dispute and quarrel over him.

anchor.quote: those in doubt are the ones who dispute and quarrel over him

prompt.en: According to the passage, God's inheriting the earth means He needs an heir to whom the world will pass.

explanation.en: The note says the opposite: God inheriting the earth means all creation returns to Him, and it seals the denial of a son, for one who inherits everything has no need of an heir.

anchor.quote: it also seals the denial of a son, for one who inherits all has no need of an heir

prompt.en: The passage reports the Shia view that the man Abraham addressed was not his real father but his maternal grandfather, since his forefathers were monotheists.

explanation.en: Tusi reports the Shia view that Abraham's forefathers were all monotheists back to Adam, so the man he addressed as 'Father' was his maternal grandfather.

anchor.quote: the Prophet's forefathers were all monotheists back to Adam, so this was his maternal grandfather

prompt.en: In the essay, what does Abraham offer to do for his father after saying a knowledge has come to him?

options.en: To share the wealth God gave him
To guide him to a level path
To build a better idol for him
To leave his father's household at once

explanation.en: The essay says a knowledge came to Abraham that had not come to his father, so he offered to lead him: follow me to a level path.

anchor.quote: a knowledge has come to me that has not come to you, so follow me to a level path

prompt.en: Tusi records that the threatened stoning was read either as pelting him with stones to drive him away or as pelting him with ____ and abuse.

explanation.en: Tusi gives two readings of the father's threat to stone Abraham: pelting him with actual stones to drive him off, or pelting him with reproach and abuse.

anchor.quote: Tusi records that the threatened stoning was read either as pelting him with stones to drive him away or as pelting him with reproach and abuse

prompt.en: "A truthful repute that God grants a person among the people is better than wealth he consumes and bequeaths." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam Ali weighed a truthful repute among people against wealth a person consumes and leaves behind, calling the good name the better portion.

anchor.quote: A truthful repute that God grants a person among the people is better than wealth he consumes and bequeaths

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, how do the two traditions divide in reading the word 'aliyyan' in the final verse?

options.en: One reads it as a name, the other as a quality
One says praise, the other says punishment
One gives it to Isaac, the other to Jacob
One reads it now, the other in the next life

explanation.en: The perspectives close that the word names a person for one tradition and a quality for the other, a proper name against a description of praise.

anchor.quote: The word names a person for the one tradition and a quality for the other

prompt.en: According to the essay, why did God give Moses his brother Aaron?

options.en: To answer Moses's plea for a helper from his family
As a reward for his discourse on the Mount
Because Aaron was more eloquent than Moses
To lead the people after Moses died

explanation.en: The essay says God gave Moses his brother Aaron out of mercy, answering Moses's earlier plea for a helper from his family, not as a reward or for succession.

anchor.quote: Out of mercy God gave him his brother Aaron, answering Moses's earlier plea for a helper from his family

prompt.en: "He made a promise to a man, and sat awaiting him for a whole year." Who said this of why Ishmael was true to his promise?

explanation.en: Asked why Ishmael was called true to his promise, Imam al-Rida said he made a promise to a man and sat awaiting him for a whole year.

anchor.quote: He made a promise to a man, and sat awaiting him for a whole year

prompt.en: How does al-Tabatabai read the exalted station to which Idris was raised?

options.en: A place high in the fourth heaven
A degree of nearness to God, not physical height
The rank of apostle set above prophet
A long life granted before his death

explanation.en: The note says al-Tabatabai reads Idris's exalted station as a degree of nearness to God, not mere physical height such as a place in the heavens.

anchor.quote: Al-Tabatabai reads the exalted station to which Idris was raised as a degree of nearness to God, not mere physical height

prompt.en: Al-Tabatabai reads 'neglect' as spoiling the prayer through ____, not abandoning it outright

explanation.en: The essay glosses the evil posterity's neglect of prayer as spoiling it through carelessness, not abandoning it outright, so carelessness fills the gap.

anchor.quote: Al-Tabatabai reads 'neglect' as spoiling the prayer through carelessness, not abandoning it outright

prompt.en: In the perspectives, al-Tabatabai records both identifications of Ishmael but leans toward Ishmael son of Abraham.

explanation.en: False. The perspectives say al-Tabatabai records both identifications but leans toward the second, Ishmael son of Hizqil, not Ishmael son of Abraham.

anchor.quote: Al-Tabatabai records both identifications and leans toward the second

prompt.en: Commentators read this not as reasoned argument but as a ____ dressed up as thinking the thing improbable

explanation.en: The essay says man's question about being raised is not real reasoning but a denial disguised as treating the resurrection as improbable, so the gap is denial.

anchor.quote: Commentators read this not as reasoned argument but as a denial dressed up as thinking the thing improbable

prompt.en: According to the essay, how does the passage answer man's denial that he can be raised alive after death?

options.en: By pointing to earlier peoples God destroyed
By reminding him God created him before when he was nothing
By recording his boast for the Day of Judgment
By threatening to gather him with the devils

explanation.en: The essay frames the reply as a reminder that God created man before when he was nothing, so raising him a second time is no harder than the first making.

anchor.quote: The answer is put as a reminder: God created man before, when he was nothing, so the second making is no harder than the first

prompt.en: According to the passage, the faithless boast of a higher station is answered by noting that God destroyed earlier peoples who were even richer in furnishings and appearance.

explanation.en: True. The essay says the boast about the better station is met by recalling that God destroyed earlier peoples richer in furnishings and appearance, so worldly comfort settles nothing.

anchor.quote: The reply is that God has destroyed earlier peoples richer in furnishings and appearance, so worldly comfort settles nothing

prompt.en: "Worship is not prostration or bowing; it is obedience to men. Whoever obeys a creature in disobedience to the Creator has worshipped him." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq redefines worship as obedience rather than bowing or prostration, so that whoever obeys a creature against the Creator has in effect worshipped that creature.

anchor.quote: worship is not prostration or bowing; it is obedience to men. Whoever obeys a creature in disobedience to the Creator has worshipped him

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, what do both readings of 'coming' to the Fire agree on?

options.en: That the believer never comes near the Fire at all
That the wrongdoers are also delivered from the Fire
That worldly wealth decides who is saved
That the Godwary are delivered from the Fire

explanation.en: The commentators read 'coming' to the Fire differently, but the perspectives say both agree the Godwary are saved; they divide only over whether the believer enters at all.

anchor.quote: Both agree the Godwary are saved; they differ on whether the believer enters at all

prompt.en: How does the commentary read God 'unleashing the devils upon the faithless' in verse 83?

options.en: As God forcing the faithless to commit sins
As God leaving them to the devils they had chosen
As the devils rebelling against God's command
As a torment reserved for the Day of Resurrection

explanation.en: The essay says al-Tibyan and Majma al-Bayan read the sending as God leaving the faithless to the devils they had chosen, not compelling them, so 'sending' is used figuratively.

anchor.quote: read this sending as God leaving the faithless to the devils they had chosen, not compelling them

prompt.en: "Fathers and mothers reckon that. No, it is the counting of breaths." Who explained the counting God keeps for the faithless this way?

explanation.en: Asked about the counting God keeps, Imam al-Sadiq rejected the counting of days that parents reckon and said it is instead the counting of breaths.

anchor.quote: Fathers and mothers reckon that. No, it is the counting of breaths.

prompt.en: At that the trees bristled and grew ____, dreading that the punishment would descend on them.

explanation.en: In the narration, when people claimed the All-beneficent had a son, creation nearly broke apart and the once-smooth trees bristled and grew thorns, dreading the punishment would fall on them.

anchor.quote: At that the trees bristled and grew thorns, dreading that the punishment would descend on them.

prompt.en: On the promise that the All-beneficent will endear the believers, what does Shia tafsir, following the Imams, identify this love with?

options.en: The covenant taken by the dying
Fear of the herd driven to hell

explanation.en: Shia tafsir reads the endeared love as the walayah of Ali, the very affection God places in every believer's heart, following the reading of the Imams.

anchor.quote: Shia tafsir, following the Imams, identifies this love with the walayah of Ali: it is the very affection God places in every believer's heart

prompt.en: According to the essay's close, the Prophet can still hear a murmur from the generations destroyed before the deniers.

explanation.en: The essay's close leaves the Prophet surveying the ruins of the generations destroyed before these deniers, unable to sense a single one or hear so much as a murmur, so the claim is false.

anchor.quote: The final verse leaves him surveying the ruins of the many generations destroyed before these deniers, asking whether he can sense a single one of them or hear so much as a murmur
